groups.contract: Admitted social duration, action ID and local-return operations
groups.disposition: Both complete 930-line bodies personally read, including fixtures; actual textual comparison has no differences. SocialDuration validates 15..480 and quarter-hour divisibility before u16 narrowing; minutes widens safely. SocialActionId uses nonempty ASCII alphabet and byte cap before retention. Local redirect validates URI, controls, slashes and backslash before emission. No operation mutates those admitted values. Fixtures read, not run.

groups.contract: Readiness, requested intent and execution are explicit separate authorities
groups.disposition: Living party members are refreshed/read one by one before leader execution or request persistence. A later error does not undo already committed condition refreshes; no cross-reducer transaction promise is present. Dead members deliberately do not block survivor actions, and only exact same-site settlement withdrawal bypasses readiness. Temporary captain delay queries current requests then approves matching actor/kind; query failure becomes an empty list and approval failures log a warning. Idempotency/authorization remains the receiving reducer contract, not guaranteed by this asynchronous wrapper. Preserve withdrawal qualification F086; no reintroduced refusal finding.

groups.contract: Party terrain profile and clock/weather inputs require their actual producer contracts
groups.disposition: Missing/dead member data is explicitly skipped. Six terrain checks derive training, intelligence and head health; aggregate is clamped 0..5 before milli-rank rounding and u16 narrowing. This makes finite normal checks fit 0..5000 but does not prove generated f32 fields finite or justify silently accepting NaN through clamp/cast; exact source admission/codec remains a dependency. Departure is a max over living member clocks, which cannot arithmetically overflow. WGS84 weather coordinate admission is explicit; signed elevation is preserved and terrain lookup fallback elevation0 is existing applicability policy. Terrain planner errors intentionally select the unplanned travel reducer; return-route errors select the same fallback before publishing any planned payload. No caller/network execution claimed.

groups.contract: Persisted route interpolation and generated SATS payload preserve unresolved endpoint/aggregate dependencies
groups.disposition: Interpolation indexes derive from windows(2), guarding empty/zero-distance/zero-duration via first point; index+1 is justified by the exact pair count. It uses a raw u64 sum and total.saturating_mul(minute.min(route.minutes))/route.minutes. At the represented whole-route endpoint a product overflow can bias progress despite saturation rather than preserve proportional distance. Example mathematical condition total>=2 and minutes=MAX makes the endpoint quotient less than total. This is pending source-qualified strengthening, not an accepted ordinary route defect: actual PartyJourneyRouteView construction, durable duration constraints and receiver continuity remain to be inspected at the types/reducer frontier. Haversine rounding/near-antipodal stability also remains qualified; no proven rounded invalid a or concrete bad coordinate supplied. WGS84 expect depends on generated persisted point admission, already supplied in bounded01-02-newmaterial-queue-087; no coverage transfer. Terrain route JSON uses the actual generated enum SerdeWrapper and checked WGS84 conversion; filters Water spans intentionally at this boundary but whole route/span coherence is a producer/receiver dependency. Fixture constructs and decodes Wetland payload locally only.
